residencyRequirements.description: At least one party must have been domiciled in Montana for 90 days preceding the filing of the petition.

waitingPeriod.description: Montana has a 21-day waiting period. No decree may be entered until at least 21 days after the respondent is served or files a response. MCA §40-4-107.

noFault.name: Living Separate and Apart
noFault.description: The parties have been living separate and apart for more than 180 consecutive days

groundsForDissolution.notes: Montana is a purely no-fault state. The only grounds for dissolution are irretrievable breakdown of the marriage or living separate and apart for more than 180 consecutive days. Montana eliminated traditional fault grounds.

propertyDivision.description: Montana courts divide marital property equitably (just and equitable). The court considers the duration of the marriage, the age, health, station, occupation, amount and sources of income, vocational skills, employability, estate, liabilities, and needs of each spouse, and any prior marriage of either party.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Montana generally divides all property — marital and non-marital — equitably. The court has broad discretion to divide all assets owned by either or both parties.

legalCitations.description: Dissolution of marriage — residency, grounds (irretrievable breakdown or 180-day separation)

filingFees.notes: Montana filing fees are approximately $200 for a dissolution of marriage. Fee waivers may be available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Financial Declaration
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, expenses, and debts

basic.name: Decree of Dissolution of Marriage
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

withChildren.name: Proposed Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Required parenting plan per MCA §40-4-212 — Montana requires parenting plans for all cases with children

withChildren.name: Child Support Guidelines Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Montana Child Support Guidelines (MCA §40-5-209)

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Montana Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Respondent must file a response within 21 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Montana has 21 days to file a response

childSupportGuidelines.description: Montana uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Montana Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: Montana requires a parenting plan in all cases with minor children. The court may deviate from the guidelines if strict application would be unjust.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Montana uses the term 'maintenance' rather than alimony. The court may award maintenance if a spouse lacks sufficient property to provide for their reasonable needs, is unable to support themselves through appropriate employment, or is the custodian of a child whose condition makes it appropriate not to require the custodian to seek employment.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Available based on need and ability to pay. The court considers the financial resources of the spouse, the time necessary to acquire education or training, the standard of living during the marriage, the duration of the marriage, and the ability of the payor to meet their own needs.

court.name: District Court
court.description: Dissolution of marriage is filed in the District Court in the county where either party resides.
